claims.text: Large language models can process and grade student responses ranging from short answers to complex essays.
Human oversight and continuous model refinement serve as strategies to mitigate ethical and bias challenges in automated grading.

evidence.description: The paper details mechanisms by which LLMs process, analyze, and grade student responses from short answers to complex essays.
Strategies emphasizing human oversight and model refinement are proposed to handle AI model biases, data privacy, and ethical standard maintenance.

methodologies.name: Case study analysis of automated grading systems
methodologies.description: Analysis of real-world implementations and case studies of LLMs in automated grading systems and adaptive testing platforms.

limitations.text: Traditional grading systems face significant challenges regarding scalability, consistency, and personalized feedback.
Integration of LLMs into grading systems introduces issues such as AI model biases, data privacy concerns, and ethical compliance requirements.

future_work.text: Advancing LLM technologies towards more personalized, fair, and adaptive educational assessment methods.
